headline: The long end is getting relief after Monday's 2002 highs: the 10Y is ≈5.28% (−3 bp) and the 30Y ≈5.63%, with Brent back under $100 and futures up 0.25–0.4%. Today's tests are the $58B 3Y auction at noon CT and Williams/Bowman, ahead of Wednesday's 10Y reopening and FOMC minutes.
summary: Rates bounce. CNBC has the 10Y at ≈5.281% (−3 bp) and Reuters has the 30Y at ≈5.626%, both off Monday's intraday highs of ≈5.34% and 5.702%, the highest since 2002. Bunds are 3.46% (−3 bp) and EGBs are recovering, even after Le Pen warned that France could default. The OAT–Bund spread is still ≈145 bp, the widest since the euro crisis. The 2Y has no confirmed live print; it closed Monday at ≈4.82%.

Oil is driving it again. Brent is ≈$98.6 (Reuters, ≈−2%) and WTI ≈$88.5 (AP, −1.1%) on stronger Middle East exports and the G7 stock release, and Qatar says US–Iran contacts are ongoing. Watch the other side too: Aramco's Nasser says ≈3B barrels of supply has been lost and rebuilding stocks could take two years. Goldman sees diesel cracks averaging >$40/bbl through 2027.

Fed path is unchanged. CME FedWatch has an Oct 28 hold at ≈78% and a hike at ≈22%, with a December hike still priced and futures implying ≈4.8% by Oct 2027. Williams speaks at 8:05 AM CT, Bowman at 9:45 AM and Schmid at 12:15 PM. Wednesday's minutes from the Sep 16 hike (+25 bp, 12–0) show how many officials want more.

Supply week: $58B 3Y today (prior high yield 4.474%), $39B 10Y Wed and $22B 30Y Thu, all settling Oct 15. Japan's 10Y sale overnight drew a 3.76 bid-to-cover at 3.115%, the highest yield since 1996. Buyers are showing up once yields are high enough, which is the bull case for this week's US auctions.

Metals are softer as the dollar holds near its YTD high. Gold ≈$4,121 (−0.4%, −6.4% on the month, ≈26% below January's ≈$5,595 peak), silver ≈$60.6 (−0.8%). COMEX copper is ≈$6.58/lb and LME 3M is $14,431.50/t. Escondida's strike is on a 5-working-day hold for mediation, and Centinela workers voted 98.7% to strike. PBOC September reserves (≈Oct 7) would be the 23rd straight month of buying if they rose.

Deals: Skydance (Paramount + WBD, ≈$110B at $31/sh) is expected to close today and trade as SKYD on the NYSE. McKesson and CD&R are near a $5B+ take-private of Bannockburn, IL-based Option Care (stock +21% pre-market, per FT). Ariel (5.4%) is pushing Mattel to explore a sale. Correction to Monday's brief: CME's GPU-rental futures did not launch Monday. The CFTC extended its review to Nov 9.

rates.title: Long end pulls back from 2002 highs
rates.body: The 10Y is ≈5.281% (−3 bp) and the 30Y ≈5.626%, after Monday's intraday 5.34% and 5.702%. Monday's ISM services prices index of 74.0, the highest since July 2022, pushed the long end up, and today's softer oil is pulling it back. Bunds are 3.46% (−3 bp) but the OAT–Bund spread is still ≈145 bp.
rates.simple: A bond's yield is the interest it pays; when buyers return, prices rise and yields fall. Cheaper oil eases inflation fears, so investors accept slightly less interest on long-term government debt. Yields are still near 24-year highs, which keeps mortgages and business loans expensive.

rates.title: $119B supply week opens with the 3Y
rates.body: $58B of 3Y notes sell at noon CT (prior high yield 4.474%), then $39B of 10Y Wed and $22B of 30Y Thu, all settling Oct 15. Newsquawk's preview had the 3Y at ≈4.96% and the 10Y at 5.30%.
rates.simple: The Treasury borrows by auctioning bonds. A 'tail' means it had to pay a higher rate than traders expected, which signals weak demand. A weak result could push borrowing costs up across the economy; a strong one calms the market.

rates.title: JGB 10Y auction draws buyers at 1996-high yields
rates.body: Japan sold 10Y debt at 3.115% with a 3.76 bid-to-cover, a strong result. The JGB 10Y is ≈3.10% (+1 bp) and Newsquawk flags hawkish BoJ sources. USD/JPY is ≈158.2.
rates.simple: Bid-to-cover is how many dollars (here yen) of bids came in for each one sold; 3.76 is healthy. Japanese investors are big buyers of US bonds. If they can now earn 3%+ at home, they may buy fewer Treasuries, which could keep US long-term rates higher.

rates.title: Real yields near 18-year highs
rates.body: The 10Y TIPS real yield was 2.88% on Oct 1 (FRED). The Sep 17 10Y TIPS reopening priced at 2.653%, the highest in ≈18 years. With nominal yields ≈5.3%, implied breakeven inflation is ≈2.4%.
rates.simple: A real yield is the interest left after expected inflation. When it is high, holding cash and bonds pays well and assets with no yield, like gold, look less attractive. It is also a sign that borrowing is really expensive for companies.

derivatives.title: SOFR futures: October priced out, December in
derivatives.body: CME FedWatch shows an Oct 28 hike at ≈21.6% (78.4% hold), down from 70.9% on Sep 28 before the +29K payrolls print. A December hike is fully priced and futures imply ≈4.1% by January and ≈4.8% by Oct 2027.
derivatives.simple: SOFR futures are contracts that let traders bet on or hedge future short-term interest rates. They now say the Fed probably waits in October but raises rates by December. That timing sets the cost of floating-rate loans for businesses and households.

derivatives.title: Bond vol is priced far above equity vol
derivatives.body: MOVE was 107.3, above 58 of the last 60 sessions (median ≈76), while VIX was ≈15.3–15.5 and VIX1D fell 22% to 10.76 (Saxo, Oct 5). Saxo's read: the front end emptied out and the back end held up.
derivatives.simple: MOVE measures expected swings in Treasury yields; VIX does the same for stocks. Right now traders expect bonds to be much jumpier than stocks. That raises hedging costs for banks and funds that hold lots of bonds.

derivatives.title: Correction: CME GPU futures delayed to Nov 9+
derivatives.body: The CFTC extended its review of NYMEX's Silicon Data H100/B200 rental-index futures (730 GPU-hours per contract) by 45 days to Nov 9, citing novel issues and manipulation risk in an opaque bilateral market. So Monday's launch did not happen. CME also shelved its 24/7 10-barrel WTI contract Oct 2 after pushback from API and BP.
derivatives.simple: The futures regulator wants more time to make sure an AI-chip rental price index can't be gamed before CME lists contracts on it. New products are how exchanges grow, but they only work if the underlying price is trustworthy.

derivatives.title: Basis trade shrinking, hedge funds still huge in Treasuries
derivatives.body: Hedge funds hold a record ≈7% of Treasuries (≈$2T cash). Leveraged basis positions are ≈$900B, down from ≈$1.26T at the start of 2026, as cash–futures gaps narrowed.
derivatives.simple: The 'basis trade' means buying a Treasury bond while selling a futures contract on it, using lots of borrowed money, to earn a tiny gap. It adds liquidity, but if it unwinds fast in a volatile week (like an auction week) it can make yields jump.

metals.title: Gold slips as dollar and real yields stay firm
metals.body: Spot ≈$4,121 (−0.4%) after a flat Monday (Kitco ≈$4,137.70). It is −6.4% on the month and ≈26% below January's ≈$5,595 peak. GLD has seen >$14B of outflows since March, while Indian dealer discounts narrowed to $14/oz from $43 ahead of Dussehra and Diwali. Goldman's end-2026 forecast is $4,650.
metals.simple: Gold pays no interest, so when bonds pay ≈2.9% above inflation it looks less attractive to investors in the West. Price dips are drawing physical buyers in India, and central banks keep buying. Those two help put a floor under it.

metals.title: Silver and PGMs give back Monday's pop
metals.body: Silver is ≈$60.6 (−0.8%) after +2.2% Monday. Parameter.io quotes platinum $1,703.71 (−1.3%) and palladium $1,161 (−1.4%), though that snapshot's timing is unclear. CME Micro Silver ADV jumped 129% in Q3 to 57K.
metals.simple: Silver and platinum are part precious metal, part industrial input (solar panels, car catalysts). They move more than gold in both directions. The surge in small 'micro' contracts shows retail traders piling in.

metals.title: Chile strikes keep copper supported
metals.body: COMEX is ≈$6.58/lb (−0.15%, +30% y/y) and LME 3M is $14,431.50/t, ≈4% below September's record. BHP requested mediation at Escondida, which puts the strike on a 5-working-day hold; the mine produces ≈3,455 t/day. Unions say Centinela (98.73% strike vote) could walk out ≈Oct 13.
metals.simple: Chile is the world's biggest copper producer, and Escondida is its biggest mine. A strike would cut supply of a metal used in wiring, data centers and EVs, pushing prices up. Mediation buys about a week before that risk becomes real.

metals.title: COMEX–LME arbitrage has collapsed
metals.body: COMEX stocks are 706,818 t versus ≈290K t a year ago, and the COMEX premium over LME has shrunk to almost nothing from ≈$420/t at end-July. LME on-warrant stocks are falling while Shanghai is shut. Managed money is net long ≈78K copper and ≈218K gold contracts (COT Sep 29; the gold figure looks suspect).
metals.simple: Earlier this year traders rushed copper into US warehouses ahead of tariffs, which made US copper pricier than London copper. That gap is gone and the US now holds a big stockpile. Those stocks could cushion any supply shock from Chile.

banking.title: McKesson, CD&R near $5B+ Option Care take-private
banking.body: FT reports McKesson (49%) and Clayton Dubilier & Rice (51%) are near a deal for Bannockburn, IL-based Option Care Health worth more than $5B including debt, possibly as soon as today. McKesson has an option to buy out CD&R later. OPCH rose ≈21% pre-market.
banking.simple: A take-private means investors buy every share and delist the company. Here a private-equity firm splits the purchase with a strategic buyer that can take full control later. Deals like this bring banks fees from financing, advice and leveraged loans.

banking.title: Skydance–WBD set to close today
banking.body: The ≈$110B deal ($31 per WBD share) is expected to close Tuesday, carrying ≈$80B of debt and targeting $6B of synergies. Class B shares move to the NYSE as SKYD. Ynon Kreiz (ex-Mattel) becomes co-CEO and Mark Thompson stays at CNN.
banking.simple: Synergies are the cost savings expected from combining two companies. With about $80B of debt, the new company will be a large, regular borrower in bond and loan markets for years. That is a lot of work for banks' capital-markets desks.

banking.title: Q3 bank previews: trading strong, advisory mixed
banking.body: JPM reports Oct 13 with consensus EPS $5.84 (vs $5.07). GS consensus is $15.39 on $17.42B of revenue, and it has advised on >$1T of 2026 M&A. BofA guided Q3 IB fees to $1.6–1.8B, down 10%+ y/y, with trading roughly flat.
banking.simple: Banks earn from lending, trading and advising on deals. Choppy rate markets help trading desks, but fewer IPOs and debt deals cut advisory fees. These results show which business lines are hiring.

banking.title: China closes a record 670 banks
banking.body: Beijing shut ≈670 banks this year, about a quarter of its banking entities and mostly small rural lenders. Fitch puts their NPL ratio at 2.8% in H1 against a 1.5% sector average.
banking.simple: An NPL (non-performing loan) is a loan the borrower has stopped paying. China is folding weak small banks into bigger ones to stop bad loans from spreading. Stress there matters for global commodity demand, including copper.

banking.title: Bowman speaks to community bankers; CRA comments due Oct 13
banking.body: Fed Vice Chair for Supervision Bowman keynotes the Community Banking Research Conference at 9:45 AM CT. The OCC/FDIC CRA proposal would raise the small-bank threshold to <$1B and large-bank to >$10B. The Basel re-proposal (≈$87.7B of CET1 relief) could be finalized late 2026.
banking.simple: CET1 is a bank's core capital cushion against losses. Lighter capital and reporting rules free up money that smaller banks can lend. That matters most in commercial banking, where community banks serve local businesses.

cnbc.title: Treasury yields ease ahead of FOMC minutes
cnbc.body: The 10Y fell ≈3 bp to 5.281% in early Tuesday trade after Monday's highest level since 2002. Minutes from the September hike are due Wed at 1 PM CT.
cnbc.simple: Bond yields dipped a little after a sharp run-up, so borrowing costs paused near multi-decade highs. Traders want to see Fed officials' notes to judge how many more rate increases are coming.

cnbc.title: Ariel pushes Mattel to explore a sale
cnbc.body: Ariel Investments (≈5.4%) urged Mattel's board to consider asset sales, a merger or an outright sale. Shares are down ≈19% YTD but rose 5.1% to $16.05 Monday. Mattel's CEO Kreiz is leaving to co-run Skydance.
cnbc.simple: An activist shareholder is pressing the Barbie maker to sell itself because growth has stalled. A sale usually comes at a premium price, which rewards shareholders and brings M&A advisory fees to banks.

cnbc.title: Trump allows tax-free 'red' diesel on highways
cnbc.body: An executive order lets anyone buy normally off-road, tax-free dyed diesel, with the federal diesel tax deferred through year-end. Diesel hit a record $6.53/gal on Sep 22, up from $3.76 before the Iran war.
cnbc.simple: Red diesel is cheaper fuel meant for farm and construction equipment because it isn't taxed. Allowing it on roads cuts prices for truckers at the pump, but it also reduces highway-fund revenue and adds to demand for a scarce fuel.

cnbc.title: Goldman: diesel stays expensive through 2027
cnbc.body: Goldman sees diesel/jet cracks averaging >$40/bbl in 2027, about twice the normal ≈$20, with US diesel margins at ≈$63/bbl. About 2M bpd of Middle East refining capacity is still offline.
cnbc.simple: A crack spread is a refiner's profit from turning crude into fuel. A wide spread means fuel costs far more than the oil it is made from. That keeps freight and airfare costs, and inflation, high even if crude falls.

wsj.title: Mattel faces shareholder pressure to sell
wsj.body: The WSJ broke Ariel's letter to Mattel's board, which argued a strategic buyer would pay a significant premium. Mattel said the board will consider the views.
wsj.simple: A big investor publicly told the toymaker's directors to look for a buyer. That often puts a company 'in play', meaning rivals or private equity may make offers.

wsj.title: L'Oréal explores offloading talc liabilities
wsj.body: L'Oréal's US unit hired Weil Gotshal and Ducera to look at moving talc/asbestos liabilities into a separate entity and selling it, as Honeywell did with Delticus. About 760 US suits were pending at Jun 30, up from ≈620 at end-2025.
wsj.simple: Companies facing many lawsuits sometimes package the legal risk into a separate company and sell it to a specialist buyer. That gives them a cleaner balance sheet. It is a niche but growing restructuring business for banks and law firms.

wsj.title: Senators probe insurers over zero-payout claims
wsj.body: Warren and Hawley wrote to six large home and auto insurers, including State Farm and Allstate. In 2025, 44% of homeowners claims at several big carriers closed with no payment (36% a decade earlier), and 45% of auto liability/medical claims did (≈35% in 2016).
wsj.simple: More insurance claims are being closed without any money paid out. Lawmakers want to know why. Tighter rules could raise insurers' costs and premiums, which matters for banks that require insurance on mortgaged homes.

tribune.title: Option Care (Bannockburn) near $5B+ sale
tribune.body: McKesson and CD&R are reportedly close to buying the suburban Chicago home-infusion company for more than $5B including debt. Shares jumped ≈21–22% after hours and pre-market.
tribune.simple: One of the Chicago area's mid-size healthcare companies is about to be bought out at a big premium. Shareholders win, and the deal will be funded with a large leveraged loan.

tribune.title: Senators press Chicago's OppFi to drop bank deal
tribune.body: Warren and Van Hollen urged OppFi to abandon its $130M purchase of BNCCORP/BNC National Bank and its national-bank application, citing loan APRs of up to 195%. Fellow Chicago fintech Enova dropped a similar plan.
tribune.simple: Fintech lenders buy banks to get a charter, which lets them lend nationwide under one rulebook. Lawmakers worry that would let high-cost loans dodge state interest-rate caps. Regulators' answer will shape how fintechs get into banking.

tribune.title: Boeing stacks defense wins
tribune.body: Boeing won the Navy's F/A-XX next-gen fighter (>$20B initial development, service entry ≈2035) and a ≈$14.7B, seven-year deal to triple PAC-3 MSE seeker output. The FAA said a 737 Max software glitch isn't a safety issue, which clears a path for Max 10 certification. Q3 results are due Oct 27.
tribune.simple: Big multi-year defense contracts give Boeing steady cash while its jetliner business recovers. That steadies a large Chicago-area employer and improves its credit outlook.

tribune.title: CME's AI-chip futures wait on regulators
tribune.body: CME's Silicon Data H100/B200 GPU-rental futures await CFTC sign-off after a 45-day review extension to Nov 9. This comes days after CME posted record September ADV of 31.8M (+22%) and record Q3 ADV of 29.4M.
tribune.simple: The Chicago exchange's newest product is on hold while regulators check the price index. CME's core business, interest-rate and commodity futures, is having record volume because markets are volatile.

nyt.title: High rates aren't slowing the AI boom, which is a problem for the Fed
nyt.body: Data-center investment is up 60% y/y and construction has more than quintupled. One estimate puts 2025–2032 AI chip, data-center and power spend at >$10T. Barclays' Rajadhyaksha argues the Fed has to squeeze the rate-sensitive parts of the economy instead.
nyt.simple: Tech giants pay for data centers with huge cash piles, so higher interest rates don't slow them down. To cool inflation, the Fed ends up hitting borrowers who are sensitive to rates: home buyers, small businesses and commercial real estate.

nyt.title: Thompson stays at CNN under Skydance
nyt.body: Mark Thompson remains CNN chair and editor-in-chief as Skydance closes its ≈$111B WBD purchase. Casey Bloys becomes chief content officer for streaming.
nyt.simple: Leadership choices at the merged media giant are being set before the deal closes. They signal how the new owners plan to run news and streaming.

nyt.title: South Korea probes AI agents in bank data breaches
nyt.body: Shinhan, KB Kookmin and Hana confirmed customer-data leaks and Yegaram Savings Bank reported ≈40K customers hit. Police assigned 28 investigators. No stolen money has been reported.
nyt.simple: Hackers may have used AI agents (software that acts on its own) to break into banks. That raises cyber-security and compliance costs for banks everywhere.

talking_points.point: Japan's 10Y auction cleared at 3.115% with a 3.76 bid-to-cover, the highest yield since 1996, and buyers came in force. Today's $58B 3Y (prior 4.474%) and Wednesday's $39B 10Y are the US version of that test. Ask a rates desk: does strong demand once yields are high cap the 10Y near 5.3–5.35%? Or do higher JGB yields pull Japanese money home and keep the US term premium rising?

talking_points.topic: AI capex and who the Fed actually squeezes
talking_points.point: Data-center capex is +60% y/y and doesn't care about a 3.75–4.00% funds rate, so the hiking burden lands on CRE, small business and housing (NYT/Barclays). For commercial banking, that means credit quality in rate-sensitive books matters more than loan growth. Bring up how a bank prices floating-rate C&I loans when SOFR futures still imply ≈4.8% by Oct 2027.

talking_points.topic: Copper: strike risk vs a 700K-ton COMEX cushion
talking_points.point: Escondida (≈3,455 t/day) is on a 5-working-day mediation hold and Centinela could strike ≈Oct 13. But COMEX holds 706,818 t (≈290K a year ago) and the COMEX–LME premium has collapsed from ≈$420/t. It's a good metals discussion: how do you hedge a supply shock when the tariff-driven US stockpile can be shipped back out? It also shows how the spread between two exchanges' prices reflects trade policy.

caveats: WebFetch was blocked, so every figure comes from search-result snippets rather than full articles. WSJ and NYT items come via Reuters/Investing.com, CNN, Insurance Journal and aggregators. Press-digest searches returned only old years, and no Chicago Tribune story was retrievable; the Chicago items come from GuruFocus, Banking Dive, Spokesman-Review and PR Newswire. Index levels are Monday closes and changes are futures. The 2Y has no confirmed live print (one unverified 4.75% quote was dropped). Oil quotes conflict (Brent $98.6–100.8, WTI $88.5–89.9 depending on time). Oct hike odds range 19–25% across sources. The trade-balance consensus ranges −$90B to −$102B. The PGM and gold COT figures may be stale. Correction to Monday's brief: CME's GPU-rental futures did not launch Oct 5; the CFTC extended its review to Nov 9.

updates.label: Close
updates.headline: Stocks closed at records, with the S&P at 7,818.93 (+0.58%), and the 10Y settled ≈5.27% (≈−5 bp) after a $58B 3Y auction that stopped through by 0.2 bp at 4.932%. Schmid's 'way to go' on inflation keeps a December hike in play heading into Wednesday's 10Y and FOMC minutes.
points: Close: S&P 7,818.93 (+0.58%, record close), Dow 51,521.28 (+253.38, +0.49%), Nasdaq 27,599.79 (+0.45%, record) per TheStreet. Nasdaq gave back about half of its midday +0.8%. CNBC's live blog had the Russell 2000 ≈−0.45%, the only major index lower (single source).

3Y auction: $58B at 4.932% vs 4.474% last month, the highest 3Y stop in about 20 years. It stopped through the 4.934% when-issued by 0.2 bp, the 4th straight stop-through. Bid-to-cover was 2.62 (2.72 prior, ≈2.65 avg). Indirects fell to 57.6% from 62.1%, directs rose to 31.7% from 26.9% and dealers took 10.7%. The headline looks fine, but foreign demand was soft: Treasury yields are ≈5% but buyers abroad still pulled back. That is a yellow flag for Wednesday's $39B 10Y.

Rates: 10Y ≈5.27% (≈−5 bp) and 2Y ≈4.79% (≈−3 bp), with 2s10s ≈47 bp (Trading Economics), so the morning call of long-end relief held through the close. The 30Y has no clean closing print (≈5.65–5.67%). KC Fed's Schmid said inflation is 'frustrating' and the Fed has 'a way to go' to reach 2%, and that the labor market is in good shape (FXStreet). That is hawkish but adds nothing new, and fed funds pricing is still ≈22% for an Oct 28 hike.

Commodities/FX: WTI ≈$88.0 (−1.6%). Brent quotes are split between ≈$99.1 (AP, −1.3%) and ≈$100.8 (Trading Economics, likely a different contract), so the 'Brent under $100' line from the morning is borderline. Spot gold was ≈$4,164 (+$24.60, Fortune, 1:55 PM ET), so it finished up after all. That corrects the midday 'flat-to-soft' read, which used a stale overseas COMEX quote. DXY ≈102.0–102.2, roughly flat, and EUR ≈1.12.

Tomorrow (Wed): $39B 10Y reopening at 12:00 PM CT and FOMC minutes (Sep 16 hike) at 1:00 PM CT, plus PBOC September gold reserves and August consumer credit. Constellation Brands (STZ, +2.4% into the print, consensus EPS ≈$3.56 on ≈$2.54B revenue) reports after the bell, with its call at 7:00 AM CT Wed.
updates.simple: An auction is how the government borrows: it sells bonds and investors bid for them. A 'stop-through' means buyers accepted a slightly lower interest rate than the market expected, which is a sign of healthy demand. Today's 3-year sale looked healthy on that measure, but foreign buyers took a smaller share than usual, which is worth watching because the US relies on them to fund its deficits. Overall, cheaper oil and steady demand for bonds pulled long-term interest rates down, and stocks closed at new highs. That helps anyone shopping for a mortgage or a business loan, at least for a day.

updates.label: Midday
updates.headline: The rally broadened by midday: the S&P hit a record ≈7,830 (+0.7%) and the 10Y slipped to 5.262% (−4 bp), while Bowman used her St. Louis keynote to reorganize Fed bank supervision into five regions rather than talk policy.
points: Rates (CNBC): 10Y 5.262%, down 4+ bp and about 8–9 bp below Monday's ≈5.34–5.35% high (the highest since 2002). The $58B 3Y auction priced at noon CT, but no confirmed result (high yield vs ≈4.47% prior, tail or stop-through, bid-to-cover vs 2.72 prior) was available at writing. Check it before Wednesday's $39B 10Y.

Bowman (St. Louis Fed community-banking keynote): she made no monetary-policy comments. She said Fed bank supervision will shift from the 12 Reserve Bank districts to 5 regions drawn along state lines, each with one leader accountable for everything, citing the SVB post-mortem. She also said fixed-asset thresholds will be reviewed later this year (Reuters, ABA Banking Journal, Newsquawk). Schmid (12:15 CT) was not yet reported at writing.

Equities: S&P ≈+0.7–0.9% to an intraday record ≈7,830, its first in almost two months and the 28th of 2026 (CNN/AP). Nasdaq ≈+0.8% and the Nasdaq 100 also hit records, with NVDA +1.3%. Breadth is wide: 386 S&P names are up, led by utilities and real estate, so rate-sensitive sectors are bouncing. Constellation Energy is +15% on the Google PPA. Option Care is up ≈33% to ≈$31.05, still below the $32.05 deal price.

Commodities: Brent is ≈$98–99 (−1–2%, AP/CNN), down from ≈$110 a few weeks ago, and WTI is ≈$88 (−1.6%). COMEX gold is ≈$4,153 (−$3.70) and silver ≈$61.0 (−$0.28), so metals are flat-to-soft despite lower yields. One source has DXY ≈101.8 (−0.35%), but that is unconfirmed. Copper has no fresh print.

Thesis check: the morning call of long-end relief is holding, and the 10Y has extended from −3 bp to −4 bp. The post-open note that gold reversed higher no longer holds; COMEX gold is roughly flat on the day. GDPNow (Q3, last 3.7%) had not been reported updated after the $105.6B trade gap at writing.
updates.simple: Interest rates on 10-year government bonds (the benchmark for mortgages and corporate loans) fell for a second session because oil got cheaper, which eases inflation fears. That helped stocks set a new record, and it helped the sectors that higher borrowing costs had been hurting, such as utilities and real estate. Separately, the Fed's top bank supervisor said the Fed will reorganize how it oversees banks: five regional teams, each with one clearly accountable boss, after the 2023 Silicon Valley Bank failure showed nobody was firmly in charge. For banks, that could mean more consistent exams. For Filip's desk, the result of today's 3-year bond sale (did buyers demand extra yield or not?) is the next clue for Wednesday's 10-year sale.

updates.label: Post-open
updates.headline: Stocks opened at records and the front end rallied: the 2Y is ≈4.80% (−3 bp) and the 10Y ≈5.29%, even though August's trade gap blew out to $105.6B, widest since March 2025.
points: Trade balance (Aug): −$105.6B vs ≈−$102B consensus and −$88.6B prior (CNBC). Imports +4.3% m/m, capital-goods imports +4.0% on AI hardware. It is a drag on Q3 GDP tracking (GDPNow updates today), but bonds ignored it.

Rates (CNBC): 2Y 4.802% (−3+ bp), 10Y 5.29% (−2 bp), 2s10s ≈49 bp. TheStreet has the 30Y at ≈5.66%, slightly above Reuters' 5.626% pre-market, so the long end has given back part of its early gain. FedWatch is unchanged at hold 78.4% / hike 21.6% (7:35 AM CT). Williams is only moderating a panel today, so the next tests are Bowman (9:45), the $58B 3Y (noon) and Schmid (12:15).

Equities: S&P +0.50% and Nasdaq +0.56%, both at intraday records; Dow +0.45% (TheStreet). Constellation Energy is up 12–15% after signing a 20-year, 890 MW nuclear PPA with Google (>$4.3B capex), with Vistra +8% and Talen +7%. Option Care is up ≈21–24% on a $32.05/sh cash buyout by McKesson and CD&R (≈$5.8B EV).

Commodities/FX: WTI ≈$87 (−2%) and Brent ≈$98 (−2%) per CNBC. Gold is $4,168.80 (+$29.30 at 6:41 AM CT, Yahoo), which reverses the morning brief's −0.4%. Silver is ≈$60.7 and copper ≈$6.60/lb (+0.2%). DXY is 102.16 (flat) after Monday's 18-month high of 102.53; EUR ≈1.12.
Deals: Skydance closed its ≈$110B WBD acquisition. WBD holders get ≈$31.02/sh cash and Class B shares now trade on the NYSE as SKYD.
updates.simple: The trade deficit (how much more the US buys from abroad than it sells) jumped, mostly because companies are importing AI equipment. A wider gap shaves a little off economic growth, but investors cared more about cheaper oil, which eases inflation fears. Bond yields (the interest rate the government pays to borrow) dipped, especially on 2-year notes, which track the Fed's next move. Lower yields make stocks look more attractive, so the indexes hit new highs. For a bank, a dip in short-term yields slightly lowers expected funding costs and keeps December rate-hike bets in check.
